subject: Renewal proposal: add reserved GPUs + SLA exception request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@orionht.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@orionht.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal proposal: add reserved GPUs + SLA exception request

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Attached is an updated renewal proposal that reflects the increased reserved capacity you requested: +16 A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool (from 8 -> 24) and a 12-month term. Key notes in the proposal:

- Throughput target: baseline throughput guarantee for 8 resizable concurrent slots, bursting to 16 for traffic spikes.
- Latency guidance: we recommend a target p95 inference latency of 120ms for the mixed prompt workload; we noted that some multi-turn chat flows will bump tail latency.
- Pricing change: incremental reserved capacity add-on is priced at a blended monthly rate; see page 2 for the tiered discount table.
- SLA exception request: because the new pool will be dedicated and sized for your expected sustained throughput, we are proposing an SLA addendum that adjusts latency SLO language and the credit calculation during the initial 90-day scaling window.

I flagged Ben and Marissa to confirm implementation timelines and finalize the SLA appendix. Can you confirm the proposed GPU count and whether you want the burst pool enabled by default?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: Orion_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf (pdf), capacity-sizing-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

----
From: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@orionht.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@orionht.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: add reserved GPUs + SLA exception request

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposal. A few clarifying questions from our infra and procurement teams:

1) Latency SLO: You mention p95 = 120ms for mixed workloads. Our product team is asking whether that can be tightened to 100ms once the pool is warmed and prefix caching is enabled. If not, we need to document the conditions where 120ms applies.

2) Uptime/credits: Given this is a material capacity increase and a 12-month commit, Orion would like more generous uptime crediting for the first 90 days if we hit rollout issues (suggested: 5% billing credit for any month where uptime drops below 99.5% during onboarding).

3) Burst behavior: If we enable the burst pool by default, what are the cost controls and throttling policies? We want predictable billing.

Priya and I will review internally but wanted these clarified before proceeding to signatures.

Cheers,
Liam

----
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: add reserved GPUs + SLA exception request

Vanessa —

I reviewed the sizing sheet; engineering can support the 24-GPU pool but we need to formalize the onboarding acceptance criteria and a temporary SLA carve-out for the first 90 days. Proposed internal approach:

- Action: Create a staged rollout plan: week 1 functional validation on canary traffic, week 2 expand to 50% of production routes, week 3 full cutover.
- Latency target: agree on a phased p95 target — 120ms during week 1-2 while cache warms, 105ms in week 3+, with a best-effort path to 100ms after 60 days.
- SLA exception: approve a one-time exception to the default latency SLO language in the contract to reflect phased targets and exclude planned scaling windows from uptime calculations.

Marissa, Jonas — please advise on whether we can accept the proposed 5% billing credit for onboarding misses or whether we should counter with service credits tied to measurable milestones (e.g., credits if week-3 p95 > 120ms).

Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: add reserved GPUs + SLA exception request

Team —

From a commercial perspective I suggest we accept a narrowed credit band but with milestone gating to reduce open exposure. Counter proposal to Orion:

- Keep a 12-month term with the +16 GPUs and burst pool optional (enabled at customer opt-in).
- Offer an onboarding credit scheme: up to 3% billing credit for a month where onboarding uptime < 99.2%, and an additional 2% credit if week-3 p95 remains > 120ms, payable once. Total max onboarding credit = 5% (caps per-month).
- Amend SLA appendix to explicitly exclude scheduled scaling windows and known cache-warm periods from uptime calculations for the first 90 days.

This reduces our recurring exposure while giving Orion predictable remedy if onboarding slips. I'll draft the contract language. Jonas — please confirm whether product can instrument the week-by-week gates and emit the necessary telemetry.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

----
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@orionht.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@orionht.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: add reserved GPUs + SLA exception request

Liam / Priya —

Thanks for the feedback. Quick summary of our counter and next steps:

- Capacity: We confirm the +16 GPUs (total 24) and will hold the burst pool disabled by default; we can enable it on a per-route opt-in after cutover.
- Latency SLO: We will add phased p95 targets to the SLA appendix: 120ms (week 1-2), 105ms (week 3-8), with a best-effort path to 100ms after day 60. We will also include language that specifies cache-warm/known scaling windows are excluded from latency credit calculations for the first 90 days.
- Onboarding credits: Counter-offer: capped onboarding credits up to 5% as follows — up to 3% for a month with uptime < 99.2% and an additional one-time 2% if week-3 p95 remains > 120ms. Credits are applied against the next monthly invoice.
- Next steps: Marissa will produce a redlined SLA appendix and send to your procurement team; Vanessa will update the proposal PDF and re-upload. If that looks good, we can route the contract for signatures (DocuSign link below).

DocuSign envelope: https://na0.docusign.net/envelopes/6a3f2b1c
HubSpot opportunity: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4950/DEAL-2026-0897

Can you confirm by EOD Monday and we will push to signature?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132
